correctness.rationale: Two distinct exhaustive C++17 algorithms, one forward on images and one backward on preimages, each enumerate all 9,765,625 ordered transition pairs and independently reconstruct precisely identical 16 reset-length triples and all 14 multiplicity frequencies. The bitmask recurrence has a direct path-to-word bijection, and the complete finite domain is exhausted. Independent brute force through length 13 identifies all 64 shortest reset words of the example, while all 240 distinct conjugate/swap automata belong to the extremal class; 240 is also the global exhaustive maximum-frequency count. Finite enumeration proves only the stated finite universe.

value.rationale: The number of distinct optimal reset controls is a natural invariant of synchronizing automata, not determined by the extensively studied shortest reset length. Complete distribution and uniquely classified extremal orbit over the first modest but nontrivial exhaustive five-state binary universe establish exact degeneracy probabilities (5,071,440 uniquely optimal versus 2,991,945 multiply optimal), show the maximum multiplicity of 64 at threshold 13 rather than at maximum threshold 16, and provide a reproducible benchmark for random automata and shortest-word enumeration algorithms. This is a motivated finite classification, not a routine extension of a previous table.
